base.description: Mast centered laterally with upper shrouds set to 22 on a Loos PT-2 gauge (jib-halyard-to-sheer measurements equalized port/starboard), then lowers tightened evenly to 14 on the PT-2 gauge. Headstay pulled straight and tight down the front of the mast, marked in line with the top of the white band near the gooseneck, then measured (mast up) from that mark to the bottom pin on the jib furler: 58 in to start.
base.notes: Headstay/rake measurement at base is 58 in (guide's own unit is inches, not converted); this does not change with wind band. The printed base-settings table also has a 'RAKE' reading of 15 (units not stated) and a caliper-measured 'HEADSTAY' field left blank for the user's own record in mm, plus spreader sweep of 2 in / 51 mm from the mast. Prebend at base (measured from back of mast track to edge of main halyard at the spreaders): Selden mast 1 3/4 in, Southern Spars mast 2 1/4 in. Colored tape marks recommended on spreaders at 18, 20 and 22 in from the mast for jib leech setup.

downwind.notes: Light air (0-7kt): ease mainsheet so all leech telltales flow 100% of the time, vang off, backstay fully off, traveller centered, boom dynamic and eased past the corner. Medium air (8-14kt): vang played to limit twist, add backstay to stabilize as breeze builds, pump the main once per wave in sync with the spinnaker trimmer. Heavy air (15+kt): vang about 50% of upwind tension, ease vang in big puffs/heel, mainsheet in close to the corner, traveller moved fully to leeward, add backstay if unstable. Cunningham and outhaul eased around the top mark and re-tensioned before the bottom mark rounding in all conditions. Spinnaker trimmed for a curl along the top 50% of the luff; ease when in doubt, trim back in when curl appears.

controls.jibFurl: 0-13 kt: furled as soon as spinnaker is up. 13-15 kt: out and loose (top quarter luffing, bottom three-quarters shaped like the spinnaker), furled through jibes. 15+ kt: out at all times to help balance the boat.

verbatimNotes: Sail with the top two jib leech telltales flying nearly 100% of the time upwind; trim until the top leech telltale stalls, then ease until it flies again — that is maximum trim.

Jib lead position measured from the front of the track; base range is 6-7 holes showing in front of the car. Pull leads back (one hole at a time) as it gets breezier for a flatter foot; push leads forward as wind lightens for a fuller foot.
Jib sheet trim marks are referenced to spreader tape marks at 18, 20 and 22 in from the mast track centerline; trim to the 18 in mark and weather-sheet the rest of the way in waves.

Jib halyard: ease when moving the lead forward (lighter wind) to keep the leech open and entry soft; tension when moving the lead aft (more breeze) to flatten the sail and tighten the leech; in windy conditions, add halyard tension to reduce headstay sag.
In 15+ kt upwind, about 10 degrees of heel is described as fast; backstay and vang on hard, traveller centered, crew hiking 100% of the time.
If the backstay is maxed out and the boat still isn't flat, consider adding more turns to the lower shrouds (within reason).
